newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore Jan bank credit rises 14.6 pct on year.
newsitem.headline: Singapore Jan bank credit rises 14.6 pct on year.

text.p: Bank credit to non-bank customers (in billions of Singapore dollars):
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) said in its monthly report that bank credit expanded at a slower rate of 14.6 percent in January, compared with 16.5 percent year-on-year in December.
Credit extended by commercial banks moderated across the board in January.
Bank loans to non-bank customers grew by 14.6 percent in January, the lowest growth rate recorded since March, 1994.
Growth of loans to financial institutions and professional and private individuals fell to 11 and 16 percent respectively in January, from 15 and 20 percent in the preceding month.
Credit expansion to the transport sector continued to slow to 17 percent from 20 percent in December, 1996.

Bank lending to the commerce sector grew by 9 percent in January, compared with 11 percent in the previous month, while loans to the manufacturing and building and construction sectors also moderated.
